anf_compare.notes: No published English was consulted; translated from the PG 76 Greek only.

bible_refs.note: LXX μὴ οὐχὶ τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν ἐγὼ πληρῶ; λέγει κύριος — same verse number in LXX and Hebrew; direct quotation.
γέγονα ἄφρων ... ἠναγκασμένος echoes Paul's Γέγονα ἄφρων, ὑμεῖς με ἠναγκάσατε; the allusion spans the end of this row and the start of ep-rem-mid; cited once here beside 'I have become a fool'.

choices.english: would also be free of shape
choices.why: Optative with ἄν is potential; the English keeps the hedge rather than stating a necessity.
rejected: must also be free of shape

choices.why: ἄποσον denies quantity or magnitude; 'size' is the plain English for that here.
Cyril means the Son, through whom God creates; capital W marks the divine Person.
The predicate ἄφρων opens the next section; the clause is completed here so the English sentence stands whole, and the echo of 2 Corinthians 12:11 is cited once.
rejected: I have become (ending the section mid-clause)

edition.locus: Ep remainder, early ('For what is free of body' to 'I have become a fool')

pass_a_gloss: For the [thing] outside body (ἔξω σώματος) would be outside shape (σχήματος) too; for without-quantity (ἄποσον) and without-shape (ἀσχημάτιστον) is the divine (τὸ θεῖον). But if they suppose that according to the nature of the human body was shaped (ἐσχηματίσθη) also the God-over-all himself (ὁ ἐπὶ πάντων Θεός), let them say if he too has feet so that he may walk (περιπατῇ), hands so that through them he may work (ἐργάζηται), and eyes so that he may see through them. Where then does he walk? Or from what sort of places into what sort does he depart, the one filling all things (ὁ τὰ πάντα πληρῶν)? For he said: 'Do I not fill heaven and earth, says the Lord?' Or what sort of hands does he move into works, the one crafting/creating (δημιουργῶν) through a living Word (διὰ ζῶντος Λόγου)? And if like us he has eyes as lying in a face (προσώπῳ), he does not at all see the things behind; but whenever he looks toward the east (ἀνατολάς), does he not know what those in the west (δυσμαῖς) are doing? And if again he looks into the west, does he not see those in the east? These things I am ashamed (αἰσχύνομαι) even to write, but because of the senselessness (ἀπόνοιαν) of some I have become [ἄφρων, 'foolish', opens next row].
pass_b_english: For what is free of body would also be free of shape, since the divine has neither size nor shape.
But if they think that God himself, who is over all, was shaped after the nature of the human body, let them say whether he too has feet to walk with, hands to work with, and eyes to see with.
Or from what place does he go, and to what place, he who fills all things?
For he said, “Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the Lord” (Jeremiah 23:24).
And what hands does he set to work, he who creates through the living Word?
And if, like us, he has eyes set in a face, then surely he does not see what is behind him.
When he looks toward the east, is he then unaware of what people in the west are doing?
And when he turns to the west again, can he not see those in the east?
I am ashamed even to write these things, but because of the senselessness of some I have become a fool (2 Corinthians 12:11).
source_text:
τὸ γὰρ ἔξω σώματος, ἔξω καὶ σχήματος εἴη ἄν. ἄποσον γὰρ καὶ ἀσχημάτιστόν ἐστι τὸ
θεῖον. εἰ δὲ νομίζουσιν, ὅτι κατὰ τὴν τοῦ ἀνθρωπίνου σώματος φύσιν ἐσχηματίσθη
καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ ἐπὶ πάντων Θεὸς, λεγέτωσαν εἰ καὶ αὐτὸς ἔχει πόδας ἵνα περιπατῇ
, χεῖρας ἵνα δι' αὐτῶν ἐργάζηται, καὶ ὀφθαλμοὺς ἵνα βλέπῃ δι' αὐτῶν. ποῦ τοίνυν
περιπατεῖ; ἢ ἐκ ποίων τόπων εἰς ποίους ἀπέρχεται ὁ τὰ πάντα πληρῶν; ἔφη γάρ "Μὴ
οὐχὶ τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν "ἐγὼ πληρῶ λέγει Κύριος;" ἢ ποίας χεῖρας εἰς ἔργα
κινεῖ ὁ διὰ ζῶντος Λόγου δημιουργῶν; καὶ εἰ καθ' ἡμᾶς ἔχει τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὡς ἐν
προσώπῳ κειμένους, οὐχ ὁρᾷ που πάντως τὰ ὀπίσω· ἀλλ' ὅταν πρὸς ἀνατολὰς βλέπῃ
, οὐκ οἶδε τί πράττουσιν οἱ ἐν δυσμαῖς; κἂν εἰς δυσμὰς ἴδῃ πάλιν, οὐχ ὁρᾷ τοὺς ἐν
ταῖς ἀνατολαῖς; ταῦτα καὶ γράφειν αἰσχύνομαι, διὰ δὲ τὴν τινῶν ἀπόνοιαν γέγονα

review_notes: Replaces a scaffold row that held no translation; the English is new, translated from the locked PG 76 Greek in translations/ac_ep_rem_source.json.
Reviewer rv0 checked the row clause by clause and made one fix: εἴη ἄν rendered 'would also be free of shape', not 'must also be'.
Questions and negations kept as questions: 'Where, then, does he walk?', 'is he then unaware', 'can he not see'.
Jeremiah 23:24 (same number in LXX and Hebrew) and 2 Corinthians 12:11 checked against the verses.
